meta: CSE '27 @ NIRMA UNIVERSITY  ·  AHMEDABAD, IN  ·  OPEN TO BACKEND & SYSTEMS ROLES

story.intro:
I build backends that stay up when traffic stops behaving.
Here's how I got here, one chapter at a time.

chapters.title: The first compile
chapters.kicker: Nirma University · B.Tech CSE, minor in Adaptive AI
chapters.text: Started a CSE degree at Nirma University with a minor in Adaptive AI. The early semesters went into fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, and plenty of LeetCode and Codeforces problems.

chapters.title: Paper to production
chapters.kicker: Radhe Engineering Works · Lead Software Engineer, part-time
chapters.text: An engineering business in Ahmedabad still ran inventory, orders and production tracking on paper. I built them an ERP from scratch and own every part of it: requirements, architecture, database design, deploys and maintenance. 20+ people use it every day, and it taught me that production is where the real requirements show up.

chapters.title: Founding engineer
chapters.kicker: Atlas AI Labs · Founding Engineer, Backend · SSIP 2.0 grantee
chapters.text: Joined an AI startup incubated at Nirma's E-Cell as its founding backend engineer. I owned the backend end to end, from service design and data modelling to containerised deploys and CI/CD, and put agentic AI, LLM and deep-learning services behind production REST APIs for healthcare and fintech products.

chapters.title: Asking satellites questions
chapters.kicker: NRSC, ISRO · AI Systems Engineering Intern · Hyderabad
chapters.text: That summer, at ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre, I built VYOM: an agentic GIS system you question in plain language, which works through ResourceSat-2/2A imagery to answer. Through a QGIS plugin it automated flood, wildfire, drought and landslide analysis across 6 disaster events and 300+ satellite scenes.

chapters.title: What's next
chapters.kicker: Final year · open to backend & systems roles
chapters.text: Final year, and still the engineer behind the ERP. Next I want a team where the hard part is keeping systems correct and fast under real load. Meanwhile I'm digging into distributed systems internals: queues, consensus and orchestration.
